title: MRI epilepsy — independent draft structure and representation requirements
counting_policy: Groups are reporting tasks, not additive completeness units. Do not multiply laterality × image/schematic/model × source class into a completion percentage. Some tasks require temporal/clinical evidence that no static 3D model can establish.

sources.title: Bernasconi et al. Recommendations for the use of structural MRI in the care of patients with epilepsy
sources.access: Official ILAE URL read as 15-page PDF with web tool; direct urllib fetch 403 is preserved in acquisition receipt.
sources.evidence_summary: HARNESS uses whole-brain isotropic T1/FLAIR and hippocampus-perpendicular high-resolution T2. Morphology, signal, architecture, cortex and relevant electroclinical information must be assessed. Fornix and mammillary atrophy can accompany hippocampal sclerosis. Quantitative interpretation needs appropriate correction and controls.

sources.title: DeKraker and Khan. HippUnfold HCP-YA Training Data v1.0.0
reviewed_locations: Dataset description, eight-value lookup table, file inventory, license metadata
sources.evidence_summary: Training tissue labels with T1w, T2w and mean b1000 in upsampled 0.3-mm hippocampal boxes; source-named left is mirrored. Archive metadata does not provide FLAIR, complete brain coverage or epilepsy pathology diagnoses.

sources.title: DeKraker et al. Automated hippocampal unfolding for morphometry and subfield segmentation with HippUnfold
reviewed_locations: Introduction; Discussion limitations; Materials and methods > HippUnfold detailed pipeline > preprocessing, tissue class segmentation and subfield segmentation; generalizability
sources.evidence_summary: Tissue classes support unfolding boundaries. Subfields are a later atlas-based parcellation. The cropped oblique images undergo affine registration, resampling and left mirroring. Resolution and segmentation limitations remain; the paper’s separate surgical case is not evidence that this HCP training subject has epilepsy.

sources.title: Glasser et al. The minimal preprocessing pipelines for the Human Connectome Project
sources.evidence_summary: HCP-YA structural T1w/T2w were acquired at 0.7-mm isotropic resolution. The later 0.3-mm training grid is resampling, not proof of new acquired detail.

sources.title: Najm et al. The ILAE consensus classification of focal cortical dysplasia: an update
reviewed_locations: MRI phenotype; integrated multi-layer reporting; Table 1
sources.evidence_summary: MRI reporting describes lesion location, extent, sulcogyral morphology, thickness, grey-white interface and signal. Transmantle signal predicts a likely subtype; it does not replace integrated classification or histology.

sources.title: Tsalouchidou et al. Temporal encephaloceles and coexisting epileptogenic lesions
sources.evidence_summary: Temporal encephaloceles may coexist with other potentially relevant lesions and may be incidental. Their presence cannot establish seizure causality or justify stopping the whole-brain search.

sources.title: Campbell et al. Detection and Characteristics of Temporal Encephaloceles in Patients with Refractory Epilepsy
reviewed_locations: PubMed abstract; high-resolution T2 detection result
sources.evidence_summary: Dedicated review with a high-resolution T2 sequence improves recognition of subtle temporal encephaloceles. A hippocampal crop does not demonstrate the middle cranial fossa floor or the herniation relationship.

sources.title: Kim et al. Transient MR signal changes in patients with generalized tonicoclonic seizure or status epilepticus: periictal diffusion-weighted imaging
reviewed_locations: PubMed abstract; study of peri-ictal MRI and follow-up
sources.evidence_summary: Peri-ictal cortical/hippocampal signal and diffusion abnormalities can change on follow-up. A static anatomy segmentation is not evidence of an enduring lesion or a seizure mechanism.

sources.title: Winston et al. Recommendations for structural MRI in infants with first afebrile seizure or new onset epilepsy
reviewed_locations: Published abstract and ILAE publication listing
sources.evidence_summary: For infants aged 1–24 months, MRI is conditionally recommended, with very low-certainty evidence. Available studies did not establish the accuracy or yield of individual protocol choices. Do not present an adult HCP demonstrator as validation of an infant protocol.

hippunfold_class_claim_boundaries.must_not_claim: Not a CA1–CA4/subiculum parcellation or complete clinical hippocampal-volume convention.
Not proof that every lamina is independently resolved, that architecture is normal, or that signal is pathological.
Not separate complete entorhinal/parahippocampal segmentations or a whole-brain cortical-dysplasia survey.

hippunfold_class_claim_boundaries.limited_credit: A boundary label used in the unfolding framework
hippunfold_class_claim_boundaries.must_not_claim: Not a complete meningeal model, skull-base surface, or CSF-pathway assessment.
Not the complete amygdala or independent nuclei.
Not fimbria, fornix or mammillary bodies.
Not a tumour, a lesion diagnosis, clinical benignity, or all cystic epilepsy substrates.
Not the complete dentate gyrus, hilus/CA4, or histologic pathology.

validation_gates.required: Pin exact files, archive member, source version, license and integrity; retain dataset class definitions.
Independently prove image/label alignment and left mirroring for this version; preserve source coordinates and registration. Until recovered, do not call the paired crops native bilateral anatomy.
Disclose acquired 0.7-mm HCP resolution versus upsampled 0.3-mm storage grid. Upsampling does not resolve new anatomy.

Show processed-grid class volumes only as processed-grid research quantities. Native patient volumetry needs inverse affine/Jacobian treatment, a declared hippocampal boundary convention, segmentation QA, head-size correction and appropriate reference norms. Do not turn a count into an atrophy diagnosis.
Independent voxel-to-mesh coverage, interfaces, topology and in-image overlays. Closedness, triangle count and finite buffers prove technical properties only, not biological truth.
Each named reportable finding requires inspectable, appropriately licensed and independently diagnosed clinical images; overlays and models must be explicitly linked to the same case/sequence.

Verify report and lesson reader in desktop/mobile, unlabelled/labelled images, original source comparison, true orientation, legible anatomy, and all source fetches. UI presence never equals clinical fidelity.
Document neuroradiologist/epilepsy imaging review of visibility, boundaries, pathology, language and limitations. No current specialist approval is claimed.

current_contract_findings.evidence: scope.json has structure_inventory null and required_not_yet_expanded for this investigation.

Current descriptors contain three remote image slots; no source_native_inspectors and no structure_atlas. Skull-base/dual-pathology and electroclinical steps have no images. Presence of remote examples does not prove rights, image visibility or every required structure.

The Focal lesions step retains a correctly identified FCD image. FCD is itself a focal structural lesion, so the broad binding is defensible; the specific tumour/cavernoma/scar examples are not illustrated by that image. Retain binding and accurate caption; an optional contextual tip may clarify its role. See epilepsy-minimal-corrections-proposal.json.
Current tip says transmantle signal indicates FCD IIb. The ILAE 2022 consensus uses probabilistic imaging prediction; wording should avoid equating an imaging sign with confirmed histologic subtype.

Module legacy reference.template offers 3-D / coronal oblique FLAIR while current reporting protocol specifically requires isotropic 3D FLAIR. Reconcile learner-visible versions without weakening HARNESS.
Walkthrough normal phrases are report templates, not evidence this HCP training subject or any atlas mesh has normal diagnostic anatomy.

non_anatomical_requirements.requirement: Record the actual T1/FLAIR/T2 acquisition, coverage, plane, source resolution and motion limitations; distinguish acquired resolution from display upsampling. Adapt age-specific teaching without claiming the adult training source validates infants.
non_anatomical_requirements.hippunfold_status: A cropped resampled T2 pair alone is not a HARNESS exam.

non_anatomical_requirements.requirement: Use supplied EEG/semiology and timing with explicit laterality and concordance/discordance/not-assessable state. A visual or 3D lesion location cannot independently prove epileptogenicity.
non_anatomical_requirements.hippunfold_status: No EEG, semiology, timing or relevant clinical interpretation for 101006 supplied.

non_anatomical_requirements.requirement: Lesion dimensions need calibrated spatial data and stated planes; clinical asymmetry needs validated segmentation, native-space treatment and appropriate reference data. Cropped-grid counts may be shown only under that precise label.
non_anatomical_requirements.hippunfold_status: Source-grid class counts are not a normative volumetry report or whole-hippocampus boundary convention.

non_anatomical_requirements.requirement: Retain normal-MRI limitations and clinical escalation fields. Do not certify absence of disease from atlas images, absence of labels or a generic model. Acute haemorrhage, infarction, encephalitis or dangerous mass effect require separately supported clinical examples and appropriate communication context.
non_anatomical_requirements.hippunfold_status: No individual diagnostic normality, negative whole-brain study or acute triage evidence.

assessment_trace.prompt: A 24-year-old with drug-resistant focal seizures is referred to a surgical programme. The only imaging is a 1.5T study with 5 mm axial T2 and FLAIR and 5 mm axial T1, reported as normal two years ago. What do you arrange?

A routine two-dimensional FLAIR is acquired at 1.0 mm by 1.0 mm in-plane with 5 mm slices. The 3D FLAIR of an epilepsy protocol is 1.0 mm isotropic. By what factor is the voxel volume of the routine sequence larger? Answer as a number to one decimal place.
A radiographer asks you to specify the three core sequences of the HARNESS-MRI epilepsy protocol. Describe them in one or two sentences, including the geometry that matters.

A coronal T2 shows a small right hippocampus with increased FLAIR signal and loss of the normal internal digitations, and the right temporal horn is dilated. Which additional finding on the same study would most support the diagnosis you are considering?
Describe the transmantle sign in one or two sentences, and say what its presence tells you about the underlying lesion.

A 22-year-old has had focal seizures with impaired awareness since childhood. MRI shows a cortically based, multicystic bubbly lesion in the left temporal lobe with a bright FLAIR rim, no surrounding oedema, no enhancement, and gentle scalloping of the inner table of the skull. What is the lesion and how should the report frame it?

A 19-year-old with focal seizures has MRI showing smooth ovoid nodules lining both lateral ventricles. The nodules follow grey matter signal exactly on T1, T2 and FLAIR, do not enhance, and show no blooming on susceptibility imaging. What do you conclude and advise?
Arrange these investigations in the order a presurgical epilepsy programme would usually deploy them for a patient whose first MRI was reported as normal.

You are planning the dedicated coronal T2 stack. The hippocampus measures 4.0 cm along its long axis and you will use 2 mm slices with no interslice gap. How many slices are needed to cover it end to end? Answer as a whole number.

A 27-year-old with focal seizures has a 12 mm lesion at the right frontal grey and white matter junction with a mixed-signal popcorn core and a complete dark rim on T2, blooming on gradient echo, with no oedema. A cousin had seizures and a brain haemorrhage. What do you add to the study and why?
Describe how polymicrogyria appears on a millimetric 3D T1 and name the associated finding that often accompanies it.

A 31-year-old with drug-resistant frontal lobe epilepsy has a full HARNESS protocol reported as normal. Scalp EEG and semiology both point to the right frontal lobe. What is the most useful next imaging step?

scope_limits: This draft expands the effective report, legacy template and current assessment obligations. Linked reading headings are context, not evidence that every listed disease is illustrated. Additional diseases/infant teaching require case-specific source and specialist review; nothing here establishes whole-module approval.
